dataset.description: The REDI project aims to investigate how managers working in multinational enterprises (MNEs) across Finland, Poland, and the United Kingdom perceive, interpret, and enact organisational principles related to Equality, Diversity and Inclusion (EDI). The purpose of collecting qualitative empirical data is to understand why resistance to EDI emerges and how managerial actions influence EDI implementation. These insights will be analysed through an evolutionary psychology lens in order to generate updated theorisation, develop more effective EDI practices, and inform policy recommendations.

dmp.description:
This project pushes the boundaries of current thinking on Equality, Diversity and Inclusion (EDI) employing a novel approach to EDI within Multinational Enterprises (MNEs). To date, interest in EDI within International Business (IB) has been largely instrumental and mainly limited to the pursuit of “performance gains or reducing internationalization process losses” at a firm level . In view of that, the aim of this project is to revise how the IB literature views EDI and to uncover how MNEs’ EDI actions can be realigned with EDI rhetoric. In tackling these issues, it is necessary to redirect the focus of EDI research from “the pursuit of diversity” to examining the value of a managerial level of analysis and the wider policy implications attached to building more successful EDI initiatives. Accordingly, the research objectives (RO) of REDI are as follows. RO1: To review the literature on EDI in IB. RO2: To collect data on the state-of-the-art of EDI in practice in MNEs. RO3: To re-analyse the state-of-the-art of EDI in IB literature and practice through an evolutionary psychology lens. RO4: To produce a policy document on EDI.

The expected scientific impact of REDI centres on contributions to the existing debate over EDI in the IB field . Beyond the academic sphere, REDI also seeks to make an impact on EU level policy through a policy brief based on scientific evidence. The expected economic impact of REDI is indirect, centring on the implied performance improvements gained from improved equality and inclusion through a more wellbeing workforce. The expected societal impact of REDI is likewise indirect, and centres on the societal effects from more equal and inclusive employment practices and policy. REDI is a first step towards building a society, where discrimination occurs less often, and equality and inclusivity are omnipresent—in line with EU’s ambition of a “fairer and more inclusive Union”.
